messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: HIGH - inference-gpu-pool latency spike detected (p95 > 2s) - triggered at 2051234567
alex: picking this up, I'm on primary for the next 30m. hitting the runbook now -> https://redwood.team/runbooks/inference-gpu-pool
maria: i'm still on the bridge for another 10m, then i need to hand to jamal. if alex needs follow-up comms i can stick around for a few more mins.
alex: thanks. quick context: customers reporting timeouts for streaming endpoints, particularly hosted-rt. autoscaler logs show repeated scale failures on nodegroup-3.
jamal: incoming shift in 12m. i can take comms once i join. alex, you drive double-checking the autoscaler and scheduling.
lee: fyi we saw related errors in kube-controller-manager: "Failed to attach volume" around the same window. could be infra-side. linking logs: /logs/infra/2051234
sam: pinging infra on-call to see if there's an ongoing maintenance. cc @infra-oncall-bot
oncall-bot: @infra-oncall-bot assigned (ping sent)
alex: running quick health check: repeatedly seeing pod create -> CrashLoopBackOff on inference-worker-*. stack says OOMKilled then node eviction. metric: node_memory_available dipping below 500MB on several nodes.
maria: runbook step 3 says to check node conditions and cordon nodes if they are flapping. alex, consider cordoning unhealthy nodes so autoscaler can spin up fresh ones.
alex: doing that now: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-3-42`. will drain after confirming replicas move.
jamal: joining bridge now. if we cordon too many we might reduce capacity further — can we bump reserved capacity on dedicated-pool temporarily?
lee: reserved capacity already at max. but we can temporarily divert traffic to regional-fallback (eu-west-1) via routing rules. that will reduce impact for some customers.
alex: good call. initiating routing fallback for streaming-hosted to eu-west: `route set streaming-hosted -> eu-west fallback`
sam: infra on-call replied: there was an automated kernel patch on nodegroup-3 15m ago that failed and left nodes in a degraded state. they're draining the remaining nodes now.
maria: customer impact note: two paying customers on hosted-rt are impacted with increased latency. flagging priority-2 and opening a short incident note for SRE.
jamal: for handoff: alex will remain primary driver until i'm fully on in ~8m, then i take driver role and maria will hand off comms to me. sam will stay available for infra escalations.
alex: current tasks I have open: 1) cordon/drain flapping nodes, 2) confirm autoscaler can provision new nodes, 3) monitor p95 and token billing anomalies. leaving a short checklist in case i need to step away:
```
- cordon ip-10-0-3-42
- drain with --ignore-daemonsets
- watch deployment scaledown/up events
- confirm routing fallback completed
```
maria: copying checklist and adding runbook pointer: Step 6 (Customer comms) -> Slack template: `/incident post "High latency - inference"` and ETA field. Jamal, use that when you take comms.
jamal: got it. i'll take comms at 2051234590 unless alex says otherwise.
lee: monitoring shows p95 trending down after route fallback. keep an eye on error budget anomalies.
alex: i'm going to step out for a quick call at 2051234610 for ~5m, jamal you will be primary driver during that time if the issue persists. leaving status: draining nodes in progress, autoscaler re-evaluating.
maria: acknowledged. jamal, i'll DM you the exact customer list and SLO impact.
jamal: acknowledged, grabbing the comms template and will post an update when i take over.
oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-20512 - High latency on inference-gpu-pool. Primary: alex -> jamal (handoff planned). Comms: jamal.
alex: thanks team. if anyone else joins, please ping in thread rather than creating parallel threads.
maria: thanks — will follow up with post-incident notes after stabilization. :white_check_mark:
